intent: The panel shown when its matching TabsTrigger is the active tab.
typical_uses: One panel of a Tabs root's content, shown only while its own TabsTrigger is active

dont_use_when.situation: Panels that should be able to show at the same time

invariants.text: `value` identifies which TabsTrigger's activation shows this panel; the root matches a panel to a tab by exact value equality, not by position.

Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, an animated panel's entrance drops the 4px travel (motion under WCAG 2.3.3) but keeps the fade (not motion under that criterion) - tabs.module.css collapses the translate to none while the opacity transition still runs.

anti_patterns.dont: Rely on an inactive panel keeping component state (scroll position, uncommitted input)
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `keepMounted` if the panel must stay in the DOM while inactive - by default it unmounts and remounts from scratch when reselected

anti_patterns.dont: Add a wrapper keyed on the active value to replay an enter animation
anti_patterns.do_instead: Leave `animate` at its default - TabsContent already replays its own enter animation on becoming active, and a keyed wrapper on top of it stacks a second enter animation on the panel's own

a11y.by: Base UI's Tabs.Panel - tabpanel role and a keyboard-focusable open panel (tabIndex 0) - exercised by tabs.test.tsx's "keeps the open panel keyboard-focusable" assertion

value.states: value is an opaque identifier, typed any by Base UI, required and matched against a TabsTrigger's own value
value.because: Base UI's Tabs.Panel declares `value: TabsTab.Value` with no `?` - required, and typed `any` by the primitive itself - so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds. It is matched by identity against the TabsTrigger whose activation shows this panel.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the panel's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the panel's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (hidden, transitionStatus, orientation, tabActivationDirection). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through tabs.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A panel matched to its trigger's value
A panel that animates its own content, opting out of the enter fade

bad.title: A panel with no Tabs root around it
bad.why: TabsContent reads the nearest Tabs root's active value through Base UI context to decide whether to render; outside one, it has nothing to read.

capabilities.name: enter_animation
capabilities.description: Default true: the panel replays a short enter animation - a fade up over 4px - each time it becomes the active tab's panel. Set false to opt out for a panel that animates its own content, or one whose content must not move at all.
